To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated the training and operation of a simple neuromorphic network using an integrated array of 100 x 100 memristors.
we demonstrate a memristor crossbar array with low variability and low power consumption that can be trained to perform a classification task.
we have experimentally demonstrated a single layer perceptrons (a linear classifier) with a crossbar array of 10x10 memristors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel technology for artificial intelligence based on the combination of metal-oxide memristors and complementary metal-oxide semiconductor technology.
the development of novel electronic devices for neuromorphic systems.

the design, fabrication, and characterization of nanoscale devices and systems that mimic the function of biological neural systems and synapses, in order to create novel computing systems with unprecedented performance and efficiency.

we report the experimental demonstration of an integrated neuromatic network based on metal-oxide memristors, with device variability sufficient to allow the operation of the network.
the authors have demonstrated the first working memristor based neural network.
the authors have demonstrated that memristors can be used to build a simple neural network, and they have done it using a technology that is compatible with the fabrication of CMOS circuits.

we have successfully trained and operated an integrated neuromoric network based on metal-oxide memristive devices.
we demonstrate a memristive neuromaorphic network that is able to learn and classify images.

we have successfully demonstrated a working memristor-based neuromorphic network with the following key features: (1) a memristive crossbar with 256 devices, (2) a memristor based synapse, (3) a memristors-based perceptron with 256 synapses and 3 neurons, (4) the memristor-based perceptron can be trained using the Delta Rule to perform the perfect recognition of 3x3 pixel images into 3 classes, and
The main takeaway from our work is that
memristor crossbar arrays can be used for the implementation of large scale neural networks.
metal oxide memristive crossbar networks, with their low variability, can be trained in a simple network, and hence are promising for the development of more complex neuromorphic networks.
the memristive crossbar technology is sufficiently mature to be used in the implementation of neuromorphics networks.
